newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese sold foreign bonds ahead of FY-end--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japanese sold foreign bonds ahead of FY-end--MOF.

text.p: Japanese investors' net foreign bond selling in February was a result of seasonal profit-taking ahead of the Japanese fiscal year-end in March, an official at the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Monday.
Japanese investors were net sellers of foreign bonds in February for the first time since March 1996.
They sold a net 450 billion yen worth of foreign bonds in February after net purchases of 502.8 billion yen in January, MOF said.
"Japanese firms seem to have sold foreign bonds to lock in profits ahead of the fiscal-year end," said the MOF official.

"U.S. Treasuries weakened in the latter half of February after a sharp rally triggered by the release of the U.S. producer price index (PPI) on February 14. Japanese firms may have decided it was a good time to take profits," he said.
The official said it was difficult to tell if the trend of Japanese investor selling of foreign bonds continued in March.
